newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom says result disappointing.
newsitem.headline: Telecom says result disappointing.

text.p: New Zealand phone company Telecom Corp of New Zealand said on Wednesday its annual profit of NZ$581.4 million was disappointing.
The result compared with $716.8 million in 1996.
Normalised earnings, excluding loss making Australian unit Pacific Star were NZ$770.5 million against $746.4 million, up 3.2 percent.
That growth rate compared with growth of 19.5 percent in 1996 and reflected a significant slow-down in the New Zealand economy.
"Management nevertheless regards Telecom's performance as disappointing and is undertaking a series of initiatives having both short and long-term objectives," chief executive Roderick Deane said.

"These are to contain and reverse the unacceptable increase in 1997 operating costs, maintain Telecom's competitiveness and margins against vigorous competition from an increasing number of competitors and to deliver financial performance which meets shareholder expectations."
Fourth quarter earnings were NZ$53.3 million, normalised to NZ$202 million, which in turn was down $12.6 million excluding the result of Pacific Star.
